tasks.short: Start machines and observe their operation, check vibration and temperature by hand, note problems in the logbook, and tell the mechanic.

steps.what: Maintenance worker starts machines and observes mechanical operation to detect problems
Maintenance worker checks vibration and temperature with hand-held meters
Maintenance worker notes problems in the machine logbook
Maintenance worker tells the mechanic about problems found

tasks.design: Wireless vibration and temperature sensors on the main drives feed readings to the maintenance system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), so the worker checks hand-held readings only on machines without sensors. Problems are reported by scanning the machine's barcode and choosing the fault from a list with a photo, instead of writing in a logbook. Starting and observing machines and talking with the mechanic stay with the worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings were taken by hand on every machine and problems written in a logbook.
tasks.enabler_now: Maintenance systems take sensor readings and barcode fault reports.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing a bearing that is starting to fail.

reach.learn: Whether reports are clear and on time.

evidence.claim: Ultimo EAM offers barcode fault reporting for technicians.
Work orders with time stamps or location can observe technicians and need works council consent first.

assumptions: Boundary: from the machine round to the mechanic told; repairs are outside.
Input contract: sensors on the main drives; fallback is hand-held meters.
s3 is part of recording machine maintenance, which sibling task 49-9043.00:11834 covers; its saving is counted there, so s3 keeps its full time here.

incremental.description: Maintenance worker checks sensors that stop reporting.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly older machines without sensors; high: main drives fitted with sensors.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Count parts in the storeroom, update the stock list, decide what to reorder, fill the requisition, check it, send it to purchasing, and store delivered parts.

steps.what: Maintenance worker counts machine parts and supplies in the storeroom
Maintenance worker updates the parts inventory in a spreadsheet
Maintenance worker decides which parts and supplies to replenish
Maintenance worker fills the requisition for machine parts
Maintenance worker checks the final requisition
Maintenance worker e-mails the requisition to purchasing
Maintenance worker receives and stores delivered parts

tasks.design: Parts taken from the storeroom are scanned onto the work order in the maintenance system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), which keeps stock current, so the spreadsheet is not updated by hand and counts become spot checks. A reorder list shows parts below their minimum level, and the requisition is built from the parts the worker picks. Once checked, it goes to purchasing in the system ({ERP}) instead of by e-mail. Deciding what to reorder and storing parts stay with the worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock was counted by hand and kept in a spreadsheet; requisitions were typed and mailed.
tasks.enabler_now: Maintenance systems book parts by scan and build requisitions from minimum levels.
tasks.still_hard: Parts for old machines have no supplier code.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which spare to keep for the one machine that always breaks.
tasks.altitude: The worker decides on reorders instead of counting.

reach.learn: Whether requisitions arrive before stock runs out.

evidence.claim: Ultimo EAM keeps preventive plans and repair history per asset.
Work orders with time stamps can observe technicians and need works council consent first.

assumptions: Boundary: from the stock round to parts stored; supplier choice is outside.
Input contract: bins labelled and minimum levels set; fallback is the spreadsheet.
Purchasing handles system requisitions as it did e-mails.
research_questions: Do repairs delayed by missing parts fall?

incremental.description: Maintenance worker scans each part taken.

approvals.approved_version: The requisition as checked by the worker in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many parts for old machines; high: mostly standard catalogue parts.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The maintenance worker keeps observing machines, telling mechanics about problems and deciding on reorders; hand readings, logbooks, counting and spreadsheets shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using the maintenance system on a phone
role.ambitious_version: A worker with more time on the machines.
